title: Introduce slack-ratio cohorter + kernel-fit allocator to reduce padding and improve kernel utilization
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Added a new sequence-length cohorting strategy (slack-ratio cohorter) that groups requests using a configurable allowed-ratio slack and a new kernel-fit allocator that picks kernels based on cohort quantiles. Reduces padding and improves throughput for mixed-length workloads. KV cache prefill scope narrowed per-cohort. No API breaking changes.
description:
Summary: This PR adds two coordinated runtime heuristics to reduce pad overhead and improve kernel utilization for mixed sequence-length workloads: 1) slack-ratio cohorter: groups requests into cohorts when max_seq/avg_seq <= slack_ratio, allowing controlled length heterogeneity to increase batch fill without excessive padding; 2) kernel-fit allocator: chooses an execution kernel variant per-cohort using weighted sequence-length quantiles instead of max-length, improving kernel fit for common cases. Motivation: previous cohorters either strictly bucketed by max length (high padding) or used coarse quantiles that left many batches suboptimal. The new approach trades off a small bounded increase in per-token wasted padding for substantially larger batch density and better alignment with kernel cost models.

Design details: - Slack-ratio cohorter: new configurable parameter 'slack_ratio' (default 1.15). Cohort membership evaluated on a sliding window per-slot. If max_seq / avg_seq <= slack_ratio the slot will accept the candidate into the current cohort; otherwise it triggers immediate flush. The implementation includes a probation micro-window for newly opened slots (100ms default) to avoid thrash. - Kernel-fit allocator: computes 10/50/90 quantiles for cohort sequence-lengths at commit time and consults a lightweight kernel-cost table produced at startup to pick the kernel variant whose expected token-cost per-step is minimal for the cohort quantile distribution. This favors specialized kernels for the centroid sizes in the batch rather than the extreme max. - KV cache prefill scope narrowing: when forming cohorts the prefill stage will only pre-warm KV slices that correspond to the cohort's 90th quantile instead of max length, reducing memory churn and prefill time. - Continuous-batcher integration: the continuous batcher was updated to expose cohort wait-time and slack-induced pad metrics to the scheduler so autoscaling and SLO accounting remain accurate.

What changed (high-level files): - runtime/batching/slack_ratio_cohorter.rs: core algorithm and probation window logic. - runtime/batching/kernel_fit_allocator.rs: quantile collection and kernel-cost lookup. - runtime/kv/prefill_scope.rs: cohort-scoped prefill logic. - runtime/continuous_batcher/mod.rs: telemetry hooks and flush policy adjustments. - tests/bench/bench_slack_cohorter.py: microbench harness and synthetic mixed-length workload results. - ci/dockerfile/runtime-image: adds tiny kernel-cost table generator binary.

Commits (summary): - aisha/initial-slack-cohorter: implement core cohorting + probation window - aisha/kernel-fit-allocator: quantile collector and kernel selection logic - aisha/kv-prefill-scope: change prefill to use cohort quantiles - aisha/telemetry-hooks: expose new metrics and unit tests - aisha/docs: add config docs and default rationale - aisha/bench: add bench harness and results

Behavioral results (bench): - 1.5x throughput increase on mixed [8,32,128] workloads vs strict max-bucket baseline at 95th latency SLO. - median pad tokens reduced by ~42% across synthetic traces used in bench harness. - kernel utilization improves for small-medium kernels (+18% utilization measured on p4d-like nodes).

Backward compatibility & config: - New config keys are optional: 'slack_ratio' (float), 'probation_window_ms' (int), 'quantile_kernel_percentiles' (list). Defaults tuned to conservative values. - No public API surface change for users calling the REST/SDK. - Runtime config update via console and private control plane included in docs.

Review discussion (abridged): - Liam Patel (reviewer): "Nice approach; slack_ratio is a neat knob. Can you add telemetry exposing the per-cohort pad bytes so SRE can tune defaults?" - Aisha: "Added cohort_pad_bytes metric and dashboard link in the PR description. See telemetry-hooks commit." - Jordan Nguyen: "Kernel-cost table needs a clear generation path; we should avoid expensive startup stalls." - Aisha: "Kernel-cost generator is <10ms on warm nodes and runs async; added an on-disk cache and a validation step to fall back to conservative kernel if missing." - Sofia Martinez: "Edge case: single large request could get delayed by probation window; ensure a max flush by time." - Aisha: "Probation micro-window has a guard: any slot that hits max_slot_wait_ms will flush immediately. Tests added."

CI & checks: - unit tests: pass - bench smoke: pass - integration (KV prefill): pass - lint: pass - perf regression gating: no regressions flagged - canary deployment: rolled to internal canary cluster for 48h, observed stable CPU/GPU counts and improved throughput.

Follow-ups (captured as linked linear tasks): - ENG-1382: explore adaptive slack tuned by traffic percentiles (auto-adjust slack_ratio). - ENG-1407: extend kernel-cost model to include memory-bandwidth penalties for long KV prefill patterns.
